subject.title: Discord compaction still fails with provider_error_4xx after #90496 closure on 2026.6.5

question: For Discord sessions whose Codex native compaction fails with HTTP 403/provider_error_4xx, should OpenClaw rotate the channel to a preserved fresh session, surface an auth/provider recovery path, or leave the session bound and require manual recovery?
rationale: The source path proves the failure shape, but the correct recovery behavior can affect transcript continuity, provider auth semantics, and channel message delivery, so automation should not choose it without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define provider-4xx recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open as canonical, run a live Discord/Codex repro, and implement the chosen session rotation or actionable recovery policy with regression coverage.

options.title: Treat as timeout-adjacent
options.body: Close only after maintainers confirm the timeout-progress fix also owns this provider-403 Discord recovery behavior and live proof supports that conclusion.

options.title: Treat as local auth/support
options.body: Defer code changes if live repro shows this is only a local expired/invalid Codex login state with an already-supported recovery command.

recommendation.title: Define provider-4xx recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as canonical, run a live Discord/Codex repro, and implement the chosen session rotation or actionable recovery policy with regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the recent partial fix and explicitly documented the provider_error_4xx recovery gap as out of scope.
